coordinate_frame: Workstation metres, +X east, +Y north, +Z up; radians; wxyz quaternions
objective: Complete the declared assembly/transport task correctly and efficiently; allocation, local motion and collaboration are Agent choices.
rules: Build the supplied Tulip reference, including background cells, one released cube per pixel. The 9x18 petal mask is mirrored from left to right. The portrait grid rotates clockwise 90 degrees as a whole on the horizontal workstation.

Cube side is 60 mm and common cell-center pitch is 81 mm. L1 has 80 mm clear square pockets, L2 3 mm red printed lines, L3 no visible grid. The four colors are cream, navy, coral and sage. The target image matches world north-up, centered on the declared assembly origin.
Stock allocations do not restrict which robot can use an item. Preserve completed placements and account for finger release/withdrawal clearance.
Only robot actuators and real contacts may affect the live task. No hand welds, object state writes, resets, hidden state tools or runtime physics edits.
The supplied pattern matrix and reference image already have their final world orientation; do not apply the historical rotation or mirror again.

completion.orientation: Cube axes aligned to workstation axes, including cube symmetries

target.supplied_reference_orientation: Already world north-up; use as supplied

family_guidance:
# Mosaic R14 task supplement

Read the assigned case's task.json and target-pattern.png. Numeric geometry and
completion conditions live in that task file; use its actual robot bases,
workspace, cameras and target dimensions. The named Mosaic skill applies to
placement, release and collaboration. The assigned role and shared robot tool
contract govern execution.

The supplied pattern matrix and image already have their final world
orientation: row 1 is north (+Y), column 1 is west (−X). Use the supplied
reference as-is. Background-colored cells are part of the artwork.

Every cell needs a distinct released cube of its required color. Source labels
describe initial inventory and do not establish exclusive ownership. Supplies
contain mixed colors to support nearby placements; inspect the current RGB and
choose useful local work as well as needed cross-zone access, staging or
handovers. There is no prescribed allocation, local percentage, color order or
transfer route. Compare total handling, reach, congestion and concurrent work.

L1 uses real recessed pockets; L2 printed lines are visual marks; L3 has no
visible grid, with the same declared assembly frame. Placement, release and
withdrawal are separate events. Later contact may disturb a completed cell;
inspect affected results again and preserve verified work while enabling
independent work with full-arm, payload and opening-finger clearance.

Track objects through permitted timestamped RGB and robot/action feedback.
Public target coordinates and a commanded TCP do not measure an object's actual
pose. This supplement contains no precomputed action sequence or Oracle
experience. Choose and revise motion from current allowed evidence.
